thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected - serving runtime errors on cluster gke-ml-prod. Alert: GPU illegal memory access (CUDA) observed on node gke-ml-pool-3. Multiple containers restarted. Auto-fallback triggered to compatible model variants. Kicking off triage — on-call please ack and start mitigation.

ops-oncall: ACK - I'm oncall and looking. Pinning logs and blocking further deploys for model_qa-v2.

mike: Looking at pod logs for model-qa-v2-5b-79f8, saw repeated failures: `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` inside libtorch. Stack traces attached below.

mike: ```
E CudaBackend: cudaGetLastError() -> CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
E serving::runtime: src/runtime/launcher.cpp:421: runtime loop crashed (segfault)
#0 0x7f2c1e0b in torch::native::...
#1 0x7f2c1f4a in cuda_kernel_dispatch
#2 0x55b3d2c in serving::kv_cache::read
```

mike: Also correlating with OOMs on the same node; kernel dmesg shows VM faults and driver messages. Possible race in page-table pin/unpin path.

eva: Which model variant and quantization were in use? Last rollout was a quantized-int8 experiment (quant-1.2). If kv cache + quantized kernels interact that could trigger aligned-mem assumptions.

mike: Yep quant-1.2 (int8/q4_0). Batch sizes ~ 64 on that pool. Traffic spike ~18:42 UTC.

julia: Proposing immediate mitigations: 1) cordon + drain the affected node to stop new pods landing, 2) reduce batch_size to 16 globally for this model, 3) rollback the quant-1.2 rollout to previous q4_1.

ops-oncall: Running commands now: 
```bash
kubectl cordon gke-ml-pool-3
kubectl drain node/gke-ml-pool-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
ops-oncall: Drain started. Evicted 6 serving pods, 2 system pods remained (daemonsets).

sre-bot: Automatic fallback executed: route model_qa-v2 -> model_qa-v2-fallback-slim for tier=free customers. Traffic shifted ~40% in 30s.

ryan: Rollback queued for model_qa-v2 quant-1.2 -> q4_1. Mike/Julia please confirm you want the rollback now, or do we stop rollout only?

mike: Do rollback. quant-1.2 has not passed our internal memtests - suspect kernel+kernel-module edge-case. Rolling back now, pausing all related rollouts.

ops-oncall: ```bash
# rollback command
redwoodctl model rollback model_qa-v2 --from-version quant-1.2 --to-version q4_1 --namespace prod --wait
```
ops-oncall: Rollback finished, new pods spin up on healthy nodes.

mike: After rollback, I still see a handful of restarts (2 pods) with the same illegal access, but they are isolated to older nodes that haven't had the driver upgrade. Looks like a cluster heterogeneity surface.

eva: That suggests a kernel/driver mismatch across nodepool versions. We should identify nodes with matching kernel + nvidia-driver versions and quarantine ones with mismatches.

julia: Created a node selector to avoid gke-ml-pool-3 for serving jobs until infra patches drivers. Also flagged infra ticket.

ops-oncall: Customer impact: early estimates - 0.8% of requests to model_qa-v2 experienced 502/503 between 18:41-19:02 UTC. Peak error window ~4 minutes. Two customers (acct:CUST-134, CUST-991) reported transient increases in latency and some failed batch requests. Notifying CS to reach out.

mike: Root cause hypothesis: concurrent KV cache eviction + quantized kernel path triggers a misaligned device pointer use after free under certain page-walk ordering; reproducible on older drivers + specific kernel versions. Not reproducible on latest internal dev nodes.

eva: Action items:
- eng-runtime (mike, julia): create repro + minimal test in lab, file kernel/driver bug if repro holds.
- infra: reconcile nvidia-driver/kernel versions across nodepools and schedule patch for gke-ml-pool-3.
- product/CS: notify affected customers and follow up with remediation notes.
- SRE: post-incident alert to update autoscaler to avoid packing heavy quantized workloads on nodes marked as legacy.

ryan: Handing off to eng-runtime for follow-up. Mike/Julia you'll own the postmortem and RCA, include timeline + mitigation plan. Ops oncall will remain looped until infra patch is applied.

ops-oncall: Thanks all. I'll keep the node cordoned until infra confirms driver bump and will watch alerts. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT status -> mitigated (reduced customer impact). Followup labels: "postmortem_required", "kernel-driver-mismatch". Escalation: infra@redwood.

mike: Adding quick note — temp mitigation (rollback + cordon) reduced error rate to near-zero. Will post replication steps to the incident doc.

julia: Oncall handoff scheduled at 20:00 UTC to @ryan for overnight watch.

ops-oncall: Handoff acked. Closing thread for active triage.
